clue.text: Half of allies will be this, beyond everything

definitions.text: Half of allies will be this
definitions.meaning: the second half of the written word allies, IES, sits beyond its opening trio of letters
in the end, when all is said and done

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about splitting one's allies, set against something lying past the whole lot.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: split 'allies' in half and IES comes after its first three letters. The second reads the phrase as 'in the end'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the end or nevertheless, and literally describes the position of IES within the written word.

clue.text: In truth Bill has a position as a minister

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill to be paid
a curacy is the office held by a curate, an assistant church minister

explanation.surface: A churchman's appointment paid for by a certain Bill, said in all honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is an account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Accuracy is correctness or exactness, which is what truth in a statement amounts to.

clue.text: The last noise maybe in a club?

definitions.meaning: the final horn blast heralding Judgement Day, in the Bible's phrase
a card of the leading suit in bridge or whist, which a club can be when that suit is chosen

explanation.surface: Wondering what the final sound heard in a nightclub might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a nightclub, but it is the card suit: when clubs lead, any club beats cards of the other suits.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical final horn call at the world's end, and a card from the suit that outranks the others in a hand.

clue.text: TV bosses show an interest in these sailors

definitions.text: TV bosses show an interest in these
definitions.meaning: audience figures that television executives watch closely
ordinary seamen in the Royal Navy below officer rank

explanation.surface: Television executives taking an interest in a crew of seamen.
explanation.definitionFit: Viewing figures measure a programme's audience; naval seamen without officer rank carry the same name.

clue.text: King to gain knowledge when knight has fled

indicators.note: once the knight has run off, its letter is removed from the word before it

parts.note: to gain knowledge is to learn
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A monarch acquiring wisdom after his loyal knight runs away.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's King Lear, who does indeed gain wisdom too late, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear is Shakespeare's tragic old monarch who divides his realm among his daughters.

clue.text: Eagerly desire to have a dreamy Oxford feature

parts.note: Oxford is called the city of dreaming spires, after a line by Matthew Arnold

explanation.surface: Longing to own one of Oxford's romantic landmarks.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford's nickname, 'city of dreaming spires', makes a spire its dreamy feature.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to set one's hopes keenly on achieving something, a strong wish.

clue.text: More unsuspecting learner taken in by silly smile

indicators.note: the learner is absorbed into the middle of the expression that follows

parts.note: a simper is an affected, silly smile
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A rather naive novice fooled by somebody's foolish grin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' looks like an anagram signal, but 'silly smile' together is SIMPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone simpler is more naive and trusting, so less inclined to suspect a trick.

clue.text: In wickedness prophet is said to be hypocritical

parts.note: taken as written
sin is wrongdoing or wickedness

indicators.note: the word for prophet is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a seer is one who foretells the future

explanation.surface: A prophet steeped in evil is called a two-faced fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: SEER spoken out loud gives CERE, the spelling the answer needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere people pretend to feelings they lack, which is what being hypocritical means.

clue.text: Say engineers will be needed on ship to provide exit

parts.note: eg, for example, is what 'say' means in 'say, a dog'
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A ship's crew needing engineers on board before anyone can leave.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, the engineers sit 'on' (above) the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Egress is a formal word for a way out or the act of leaving.

clue.text: Enclosed area in which one may see car dry out

indicators.note: what one may see in these words is the answer, once their letters are rearranged

parts.note: the three words provide the nine letters to be shuffled

explanation.surface: A walled yard where someone might watch a car drying off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' reads as part of drying the car but is fodder too: all nine letters of CAR DRY OUT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtyard is an open space surrounded by walls or buildings.

clue.text: I repeatedly snored dreadfully — a laughing stock

indicators.note: done dreadfully, the letters are jumbled into a new order
the letter I is to be used twice over

explanation.surface: Someone confessing their terrible snoring has made them a figure of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Two I's and SNORED are mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Derision is mockery, and the term can loosely stand for the object of ridicule, someone jeered at.

clue.text: Male is having hesitation — not the most generous fellow!

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating speech

explanation.surface: A man hesitating, it seems, because he is reluctant to pay up.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hoards money and hates spending, the opposite of a generous person.

clue.text: Show remorse as initiators of ruthless enterprise, then shut up

indicators.note: the starting letters of the next two words are taken

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means confined

explanation.surface: Regretting a ruthless business venture and then keeping quiet about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' is not a command but an adjective, confined.
explanation.definitionFit: To repent is to feel and display sorrow for one's wrongdoing.

clue.text: Gentle pieces of poetry enthralling artist — they are sweet

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for soft or gentle
lines are units of a poem
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Soft verses captivating a painter, with a note that they are charming.
explanation.walkthrough: P from 'Gentle' and LINES make the outer piece, which holds RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Pralines are confections of nuts cooked in sugar, so they are sweets.

clue.text: I am some sort of dog, little fellow to be opposed

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
a pug is a small breed of dog
Ned is a short form of Edward, a fellow's name

explanation.surface: A speaker announcing they are a breed of dog, a small chap who must be resisted.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn a claim is to challenge or dispute it, so impugned means contested or opposed.

clue.text: Smart heretics ruined a feature of the festive season

definitions.text: a feature of the festive season

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Clever dissenters have spoiled the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: SMART HERETICS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorated fir in the living room is a standard sight during the December holidays.

clue.text: Wounded grenadier is studying again

indicators.note: wounded means damaged, so the letters of the soldier are rearranged

explanation.surface: An injured soldier is going back over his books.
explanation.walkthrough: GRENADIER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Rereading a text means going over it once more, a way of studying it a second time.

clue.text: It presents a purple colour — as may the drunk on street

indicators.note: being drunk means in a muddle, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Something showing violet, like a drinker out on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: MAY THE is rearranged before ST. The stone's name comes from Greek for 'not drunken', since it was thought to prevent intoxication.
explanation.definitionFit: The amethyst is a violet variety of quartz used as a gemstone.

clue.text: Lose enthusiasm, as one deprived of heat and water could

definitions.meaning: to tire and lose one's drive

definitions.text: one deprived of heat and water could
definitions.meaning: steam is water plus heat, so lacking both leaves one with literally none

explanation.surface: Flagging, as a body without warmth or drink would.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: heated water is steam, so lacking both means having no steam left.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for flagging comes from steam engines slowing as pressure fails, hence tiring and giving up.

clue.text: Candidate has no source of wealth before start of election

indicators.note: before places the source of wealth ahead of the following letter

parts.note: taken as written
a gold mine is a rich source of wealth

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A political hopeful who has no money as an election begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is someone put forward for a post or award, i.e. a contender.

clue.text: Court is thus within the law

parts.note: so means thus or in this way
licit means lawful

explanation.surface: A statement that a legal tribunal operates lawfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a law court but is the verb, to woo or seek.
explanation.definitionFit: To court support or attention is to seek it or ask for it, as when one canvasses.

clue.text: City den supplying cake

parts.note: EC is the postal district of the City of London, its financial centre
a lair is an animal's den

explanation.surface: A town's hideaway serving up a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger of choux pastry filled with cream and iced, a small cake.

clue.text: Delightful cleaner of a bygone time in China

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a British cleaning lady
the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644

explanation.surface: A lovely domestic help from an ancient Chinese era.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR is old-fashioned British for a woman hired to clean houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming describes someone pleasing and attractive, giving delight.

clue.text: Come down in flames

definitions.meaning: to get off a vehicle or descend and land

explanation.surface: Crashing to earth while burning.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the verb to land or dismount; the other is the adjective meaning on fire.

clue.text: A horse topples over traversing hard country

indicators.note: traversing means lying across, so the turned piece spans the letter for hard
in a down clue toppling over turns the words upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: a nag is a horse
H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A horse falls while crossing rough ground in some nation.
explanation.walkthrough: A NAG reversed gives GANA, which goes around H.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana is a nation of West Africa, formerly the Gold Coast.

clue.text: A war medal, something circular that is given to a soldier

definitions.text: that is given to a soldier

parts.note: MM is the Military Medal, a British award for bravery
the letter O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A decoration and a round token handed to a serviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammunition, the bullets and shells issued to troops, is what a fighting man is supplied with.

clue.text: Stranger story embedded within article

indicators.note: the story is set inside the article

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a story can be a lie, a fib

explanation.surface: An odder tale tucked inside a newspaper feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' looks like an adjective, odder, but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a foreigner or outsider, someone unknown in a place.

clue.text: Protest about naughty form of government

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
c, circa, means about
racy means risque or naughty

explanation.surface: Demonstrating against a slightly risque political system.
explanation.definitionFit: Democracy is rule by the people through elected representatives, a political system.

clue.text: Having a floor covering that is rough

definitions.meaning: furnished with a mat or carpet

explanation.surface: A carpeted room that is nevertheless coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is fitted with a mat, the other means uneven or craggy, as terrain.

clue.text: Picture of foreign river — river with distinguishing feature

parts.note: the Po is a river in Italy
a trait is a characteristic feature

explanation.surface: A painting of an overseas river that has a notable characteristic.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painting or photograph of a person, a likeness.
